sentences.text: Explorornis is a genus of Mesozoic birds named after the Latin word for 'to discover' and the Greek word for 'bird'.
Most species were small birds about 15 to 20 cm long, while E. walkeri was likely over 25 cm long.
The two species of Explorornis are named after paleontologists Lev Alexandrovich Nesov and Alick Donald Walker.
The phylogenetic position of Explorornis is unresolved because only coracoid fossils are known.
Explorornis belongs to the parent group Alexornithidae.
Explorornis is classified within the family Alexornithidae.
Explorornis is classified under the class Reptilia.
Explorornis lived around 90 million years ago during the mid-late Turonian stage in the Bissekty Formation of the Kyzyl Kum in present-day Uzbekistan.
The animal lived between 93.9 and 89.8 million years ago during the Turonian stage.
